title: Guess’ European Fulfillment Operation Gets a Robotic Upgrade
excerpt: GXO is deploying 127 Exotec Skypod robots at the fashion retailer's Netherlands distribution center to reduce manual picking and support e-commerce growth ac...
content_html:
Glenn Taylor

Wed, September 16, 2026 at 8:00 AM CDT 4 min read

Guess is layering new levels of robotics into its European fulfillment network.

GXO, which operates three warehouses for Guess, is implementing 127 Skypod robots from warehouse robotics company Exotec at a distribution center in Venlo, the Netherlands, as the contract logistics provider looks to more efficiently handle the apparel brand's complex mix of seasonal inventory.

An automated system, supplied and integrated by Exotec, has been deployed at GXO's Venlo facility, which has handled logistics operations for Guess since 2017. The operation distributes merchandise to Guess stores across Europe, the Middle East and Africa and Asia (EMEA), while preparing to launch e-commerce fulfillment for customers in the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg.

The GXO partnership and automation upgrades enable Guess to absorb additional volume and new e-commerce flows within an established operation without requiring the fashion brand to undergo a complete warehouse redesign.

The system combines the Skypod robots with 60,000 storage locations, eight goods-to-person picking stations and a conveyor system stretching roughly 650 feet. At peak, it can process 2,200 order lines per hour and between 40,000 and 70,000 pieces per day, according to Exotec.

For GXO, the investment is aimed at addressing a familiar problem in fashion logistics: an operation that needs to be simultaneously flexible enough to handle thousands of SKUs and seasonal swings while maintaining the speed and accuracy required across multiple sales channels.

"We were looking for solutions to automate. The question was: how can we reduce the picking effort?" said Mark Donné, operations manager at GXO Venlo.

Rather than adding automation to the existing workflow, GXO and Exotec designed the system around the specific requirements of the Guess operation. Exotec served as the integrator, combining storage, robotics, picking and material handling into a single system.

The Skypod robots move through the storage structure to retrieve inventory and bring it to operators at the picking stations, replacing much of the walking associated with traditional warehouse picking.

According to Exotec, the robots carry loads of up to 30 kilograms in bins, trays or custom containers, travel at up to four meters per second in three dimensions, climb racks up to 46 feet, operate in temperatures from zero to 40 degrees Celsius and can drive beneath the racks in any direction.
